newsitem.title: UK: EMU expectations stable in latest week - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: EMU expectations stable in latest week - JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations of a broad-based start to European monetary union in 1999 were little changed last week, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed.

Financial prices indicate that the probability assumed by the market of Italy and Spain joining Germany and France in the first wave of EMU dipped slightly during the week, according to the U.S. investment firm's "EMU calculator." Both country's readings were still higher than a month ago though.
The probability of Italy starting EMU in 1999 dropped one point to 52 percent, and Spain also eased one point to 67 percent. Sweden fell three points to 56 percent this week.
The calculator showed the probability of France and Belgium starting EMU remains 100 percent.
JP Morgan point out there is a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of between three and five points.

Elsewhere, expectations of first-wave EMU participation by Denmark rose 10 to 54 percent, while Portugal was up one to 72 percent. The UK was down four at 34 percent and Ireland dropped three to 59. Finland dropped one to 76 percent.
JP Morgan's EMU calculator is derived from the interest rate swaps market.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
